issues: Integrity: no problems found. There is no file or network access and no pasted answers. Labels are used only through train_y. The bootstrap indexes only the training kernel (Ktr[np.ix_(idx, idx)]) and the test-to-train columns (Kte[:, idx]).

Bugs: none found. Duplicate rows and columns in a precomputed SVR kernel are valid. Randomness comes from the seed argument (seed + b). Averaging the ranks of each bootstrap model and then ranking again in the final blend is redundant but harmless.
Effectiveness: each bootstrap fit sees only about 63% of the unique training molecules, which probably weakens the SVR. Three bags are too few to make up for that, so a small loss is expected.

Numbers: z recomputed as (0.4718 - 0.4745) / (0.0070 * sqrt(2)) = -0.27, which matches the reported -0.270. A 0.0027 increase in loss is within noise. The candidate is not better and adds code, so reject is the right call.
